title: Set 147

sentences.ko: 그러니까 그 사람 간호사라서 밤에 일하거든. 그래서 오후 두 시에 문자 답장이 없어도 너한테 관심이 없어서 그런 게 아니야. 그냥 자고 있는 거야. 근데 솔직히 내가 아는 남자 중에 손꼽히게 착한 애야.
sentences.text: Okay, so he's a nurse and he works nights, so if he doesn't text you back at two in the afternoon, it's not because he's not into you, he's just asleep. But honestly, he's one of the nicest guys I know.

alts.text: He's a nurse on night shift, so if you don't hear back at 2 p.m., he's not blowing you off, he's asleep. Seriously though, he's one of the nicest guys I know.

He is a nurse who works night shifts, so if he does not reply to your message at two in the afternoon, it is not because he is uninterested; he is simply asleep. In all honesty, he is one of the kindest people I know.

sentences.note: **works nights** 는 밤에 일한다, 야간 근무를 한다는 뜻이에요. **not into you** 는 너한테 관심이 없다는 구어 표현이고, casual 의 **blowing you off** 는 일부러 무시한다는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 그 제빵기 주말마다 쓸 줄 알았는데, 빵을 딱 한 번 만들었어. 이제는 조리대 위에서 자리만 차지하고 있어. 반품도 못 해. 상자를 벌써 버렸거든.
sentences.text: I really thought I'd use that bread maker every weekend, but I've made exactly one loaf, and now it just sits on the counter taking up space. And I can't even return it, because I already threw out the box.

alts.text: Figured I'd use that bread maker every weekend. Made one loaf. One. Now it's just sitting on the counter hogging space, and I can't return it 'cause I tossed the box.

I truly believed I would use that bread maker every weekend, but I have made only one loaf, and it now sits on the counter taking up space. I am unable to return it, as I have already discarded the box.

sentences.note: **taking up space** 는 괜히 자리만 차지한다는 뜻이에요. **threw out** 은 버렸다는 말이고, casual 의 **hogging space** 는 자리를 독차지한다는 더 투덜대는 말투예요.

sentences.ko: 파머스 마켓까지 걸어가려고 했는데, 아침 아홉 시인데 벌써 화씨 90도쯤 되더라고. 그래서 그냥 차 타고 마트로 갔고, 그날은 내내 에어컨 켜 놓고 집 안에만 있었어.
sentences.text: We were going to walk to the farmers market, but it was already like ninety degrees at nine in the morning, so we just drove to the grocery store instead and stayed inside with the AC the rest of the day.

alts.text: We were gonna walk to the farmers market, but it was like ninety degrees by nine a.m., so we just drove to the grocery store and hid out inside with the AC all day.

We had planned to walk to the farmers market, but it was already about ninety degrees at nine in the morning, so we drove to the grocery store instead and remained indoors with the air conditioning for the rest of the day.

sentences.note: **like ninety degrees** 의 like 는 대충, 한 ~쯤이라는 뜻으로 말할 때 자주 붙여요. casual 의 **hid out** 은 어디에 피신해 숨어 있었다는 느낌이에요.

sentences.ko: 우리 개는 원래 청소기를 무서워했어. 그건 이해해. 근데 이제는 대걸레까지 무서워해. 둘을 같은 수납장에 넣어 둬서 그런 것 같아. 그래서 내가 그 문만 열면 뛰어가서 침대 밑에 숨어.
sentences.text: Our dog's always been scared of the vacuum, which I get, but now he's scared of the mop too, and I think it's because I keep them in the same closet. So every time I open that door, he runs and hides under the bed.

alts.text: The vacuum's always freaked out our dog, fair enough, but now it's the mop too. Probably 'cause they're in the same closet. I open that door and he bolts under the bed.

Our dog has always been afraid of the vacuum cleaner, which I understand, but he is now afraid of the mop as well. I believe it is because I keep them in the same closet, so whenever I open that door, he runs and hides under the bed.

sentences.note: **which I get** 은 그건 이해한다고 앞말에 짧게 덧붙이는 말이에요. casual 의 **bolts** 는 쏜살같이 달아난다는 뜻이고, **freaked out** 은 기겁하게 만들었다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 우리 동네 정말 좋아. 진짜로. 근데 애들이 곧 각자 방이 있어야 하는데, 여기서는 도저히 안 돼. 문제는 이사하면 애들이 전학을 가야 한다는 거야. 우리 딸이 이제 겨우 친구를 좀 사귀었거든.
sentences.text: I love our neighborhood, I really do, but the kids are going to need their own rooms soon, and we just can't make that work here. The thing is, if we move, they'd have to switch schools, and my daughter just finally made some friends.

alts.text: Honestly, I love it around here, but the kids are gonna need their own rooms soon and it's just not doable here. Problem is, moving means new schools, and my daughter finally made some friends.

I am very fond of our neighborhood, but the children will soon need rooms of their own, and that is simply not possible in our current home. However, if we move, they would have to change schools, and my daughter has only recently made some friends.

sentences.note: **make that work** 는 어떻게든 되게 한다는 뜻이에요. **The thing is** 는 문제는 말이야 하고 핵심을 꺼낼 때 쓰고, **switch schools** 는 전학 간다는 말이에요.

reviewed: 1번 한국어의 '제일 착한 사람 중 하나야'는 영어 one of the nicest를 그대로 옮긴 번역투라서 '손꼽히게 착한 애야'로 고쳤습니다.
3번 casual의 hid out in the AC는 에어컨 안에 숨었다는 식으로 어색하게 들려서 hid out inside with the AC로 고쳤고, note도 여기에 맞췄습니다.
